record.paper_title: Open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases with zero-range interactions
record.original_question: Can Landau-Khalatnikov four-phonon damping φφ → φφ be observed and quantitatively measured in a superfluid whose acoustic branch is concave at low wave number, γ < 0, such as a strongly interacting Fermi gas in a box trap or superfluid helium-4 under pressure? The target is the low-temperature regime where phonon decay into multiple phonons is kinematically forbidden and four-phonon scattering is predicted to dominate over three-phonon Beliaev-Landau damping.

evidence.quote: To our knowledge, this four-phonon damping has not yet been observed experimentally in any system. It could be observed in a Fermi gas of cold atoms in a box trap [72]. It could also be observed in superfluid helium-4

this case has been little studied theoretically (reference [78] noted and corrected an error in the original calculation [52], and reference [86] obtained a much more explicit expression of the result, even generalizing it to a non-zero phonon chemical potential µφ) and it has, to our knowledge, never been observed experimentally (no precise measurement of Γγ<0 q has been made in any system).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a three-dimensional superfluid at low temperature whose elementary excitations include an acoustic (phonon) branch with dispersion relation ω(q) = c q [1 + (γ/8)(ℏq/mc)^2 + O(q^4)] for small wave number q, where c is the sound velocity, m a characteristic mass, and γ the dimensionless curvature parameter. Assume γ < 0 (concave start of the dispersion), so that one-phonon decay into two phonons (Beliaev process) and merging of two phonons into one (Landau process) are kinematically forbidden at low q, and the leading damping mechanism is the Landau–Khalatnikov four-phonon process φφ → φφ. The corresponding damping rate Γ_q^{γ<0}(T) at temperature T has been predicted theoretically (in the regime ℏcq, k_B T much smaller than the characteristic gap or roton scale).

Two physical realizations satisfy γ < 0: (i) a unitary (or strongly interacting) Fermi gas of paired atoms confined in a uniform box trap, in the collisionless low-temperature regime; (ii) bulk superfluid helium-4 under sufficiently high pressure.

Problem: Devise an experimental protocol in one of these two systems that allows the four-phonon damping rate Γ_q^{γ<0}(T) of a phonon mode of wave number q to be observed and quantitatively measured at low temperature, where three-phonon Beliaev–Landau processes are kinematically forbidden, and compare the measured rate against the theoretical prediction.
artifact.status_search_result: Theoretical predictions for the four-phonon Landau–Khalatnikov damping rate exist for strongly interacting Fermi gases and high-pressure superfluid helium-4 (concave acoustic branch, γ < 0), but available sources indicate that this four-phonon damping has not yet been observed experimentally in any system; its measurement remains an open experimental challenge.

status_evidence.title: Landau-Khalatnikov phonon damping in strongly interacting Fermi gases
status_evidence.snippet: Predictions apply throughout the BEC-BCS crossover where the phononic dispersion has a concave start, paving the way to experimental observation.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical prediction exists; experimental observation is anticipated but not yet realized.

status_evidence.title: Landau Phonon-Roton Theory Revisited for Superfluid 4He and Fermi Gases
status_evidence.snippet: Phonon damping rates are calculated at low temperature in high-pressure liquid helium and in strongly interacting Fermi gases.
status_evidence.claim: High-pressure helium-4 and unitary Fermi gases are proposed candidates for measuring four-phonon damping.

status_evidence.title: Phonon-roton coupling in liquid helium and in superfluid Fermi gases - LKB
status_evidence.snippet: Observation of Landau-Khalatnikov phonon damping would be unprecedented.
status_evidence.claim: As of the available sources, four-phonon Landau–Khalatnikov damping has not been observed.
